Subject: Plan guidance for pilot -> prod path

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Luma loved the latency profile and the traceability features in Redwood Console. We're approaching internal approval and I wanted to get sharper on packaging so we can recommend a path to procurement.

Two quick asks:
- For a 3-month pilot (50k tokens/day average, occasional bursts), which plan do you recommend: Hosted (metered) + Optimize add-on, or a small Dedicated pool? Cost and operational risk (downtime during ramp) are our top concerns.
- If we start on Hosted and later switch to Dedicated, what does the downgrade/upgrade path look like? Any commitment hold/credits we should be aware of?

Also, procurement asked for a one‑page comparison and a draft proposal we can share. Can you send those?

Best,

Luma Health

Hi Elena — great to hear the demo landed well. Short answers up front, details below and I've attached a pricing grid + draft pilot proposal.

Recommendation (pilot): Hosted (metered) + Optimize + Console retention at 90 days. Why: fastest time-to-value, no upfront commit, and Optimize can drive down token cost by ~20-30% for your query mix during pilot.

When to pick Dedicated: if you need strict throughput guarantees (SLA), guaranteed GPU concurrency for synchronous workloads, or strict data isolation (customer-managed VPC). For a 50k token/day pilot, Dedicated usually isn't cost-effective unless you require 99.9% per-route latency SLOs.

Upgrade path (Hosted -> Dedicated):
- We run the pilot on Hosted and collect telemetry (latency, qps, token mix).
- At decision time we propose a Dedicated sizing based on observed P50/P95 and KV-cache hit rate.
- Transition is supported with minimal downtime — model variants are pinned and we can warm KV caches.

Commit/credits: if you convert to Dedicated within 90 days of the pilot, we can apply a one-time onboarding credit equal to 15% of the first 3 months' committed value (deal-specific). If you back out after provisioning Dedicated, there's a standard 30-day notice and prorated refund on unused committed funds per contract terms.

I've attached: pricing_grid_v3.xlsx (simple cost models for Hosted vs Dedicated) and pilot_proposal_draft.pdf (one-pager + SLAs). See link to the HubSpot record in case you want us to attach the draft to vendor review.

Next step: Are you available Wednesday 7/21 10am PT for a 30m procurement walk-through?

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher

Hi Elena — Monica from Solutions/Onboarding here. A couple of operational notes to add to Sean's high-level guidance: 

- If you choose Hosted: we recommend enabling prefix/KV caching and a 3-day warmup window on the first week of the pilot to stabilize latency metrics. That avoids over-provisioning later.
- For Dedicated sizing: we base the GPU footprint on P95 tokens-per-second and cache hit percentages. Practically, a small Dedicated pool (1-2 GPU equivalent) would be the recommended next step if you hit sustained 75k+ tokens/day during the pilot.
- Downgrade sensitivity: commits on Dedicated are term-based. Customers can reduce capacity at renewal, but mid-term reduction triggers a short-term credit/fee schedule. We can model a cushion/burst buffer to avoid mid-term resizing.

I can run a quick sizing exercise if you share a week's request logs (masked) or allow us to instrument telemetry during the pilot.

Happy to cover this in the Wednesday call.

Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Elena Morales <elena@lumahealth.com>

Thanks Sean and Monica — really helpful. A few clarifying items from procurement: 

1) That 15% onboarding credit — is it applied as a rebate on the first invoice or as an offset against committed funds? Procurement prefers a line-item discount on the first invoice.
2) If we start on Hosted and later sign Dedicated, will Dedicated include Console + Optimize by default or are those separate add-ons? We need to know which items are included so we can build an apples-to-apples TCO.
3) Downgrade language: can you provide the standard contract text or a short snippet we can attach to the draft? Procurement wants the exact phrasing about prorated refunds and notice periods.

We can do the 7/21 10am PT meeting but procurement will likely want someone from legal/joint procurement on the call. Can you send an updated one-pager that explicitly lists included modules per plan?

Best,
Elena

Hi Elena — quick answers inline and we'll update the one-pager before the call.

1) Onboarding credit: We can surface it as a line-item credit on the first invoice (preferred) — we'll put the 15% rebate in the SOW/quote as a discrete credit so procurement can see it clearly.

2) Included modules: Dedicated includes the base Redwood Console (standard observability) and the serving runtime. Optimize and some advanced retention/alerts are licensed as add-ons. We'll produce an apples-to-apples TCO table (Hosted vs Dedicated) that marks which modules are included vs add-on and approximate pricing bands.

3) Contract text: attaching a short excerpt below that procurement can paste into their bundle (we'll also provide the full contract excerpt before signature):

--- Contract excerpt (summary) ---
If Customer terminates or reduces committed capacity mid-term, Redwood will provide a prorated refund on unused committed fees calculated on a 30-day basis, less any onboarding credits applied. A 30-day written notice is required for capacity reductions. Specific refund schedules vary by region and currency and will be defined in the Master Services Agreement (MSA).

We'll circulate the updated one-pager + a version of the SOW with the credit called out by EOD tomorrow so you have it ahead of the call. Who should I expect from procurement on the call?

Thanks,
